headline: Taiwan's science council has announced the next five-year phase of its national quantum programme, inviting teams to build a working quantum computer and a long-distance quantum network.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a government programme with a clear goal, but no budget for the new phase is reported and no teams are chosen yet.
importance_line: Taiwan's quantum researchers and chip-industry partners could get another five years of state backing, but the Commercial Times gives no budget for the new phase and this is a call for proposals, not yet a set of awards.
summary: Taiwan's Commercial Times reports that the National Science and Technology Council has opened applications for the second phase of its National Quantum Team programme, which encourages teams to build a working quantum computer and a long-distance quantum communication network within five years. Digitimes, which carries the announcement in English, says the first phase, a NT$8 billion (about US$252 million) project, ends in 2026; the Commercial Times says the new phase is meant to speed industry use, building on Taiwan's chip-making strengths.
notes: Pool item is Digitimes (6 Oct 2026), readable only to its first paragraph (subscription wall); no other English outlet found. Details read in the Chinese-language Commercial Times (5 Oct 2026), so it is credited and linked as the source; Digitimes is named in the summary. Exact date of the NSTC announcement not stated, first reports 5 Oct 2026, so kept NEW. English names are our translation. No budget figure for phase two found. Meaning check: call for proposals, five-year goal (working hardware plus long-distance quantum network), first-phase cost and end date, chip-industry link all kept; no award or budget claimed.
